name: Quibi
one_line_pitch: Premium short-form mobile video episodes built for commuters and phone-first viewing.
primary_failure_reason: Misread consumer demand, pricing tolerance, and mobile viewing habits while launching into a crowded streaming market.
key_lessons: Validate a durable user habit before committing to massive content spend
Do not confuse celebrity supply with customer demand
A launch context can erase the use case a product depends on

name: Juicero
one_line_pitch: A connected countertop press for squeezing proprietary fresh juice packs.
primary_failure_reason: Expensive hardware did not create enough value beyond squeezing the packs by hand.
key_lessons: Prove the hardware performs a necessary job better than simple alternatives
Avoid proprietary consumables unless the customer value is obvious
Overengineering can turn a convenience product into a punchline

name: Theranos
one_line_pitch: Blood testing from tiny samples through compact proprietary diagnostic machines.
primary_failure_reason: Technical claims outran validated science and regulatory reality in a high-trust healthcare market.
key_lessons: Healthcare products require evidence before scale
Secrecy cannot substitute for technical validation
Governance must challenge charismatic founders in regulated markets

name: Webvan
one_line_pitch: Online grocery ordering with rapid home delivery from automated fulfillment centers.
primary_failure_reason: Expanded capital-intensive logistics before demand density and unit economics were proven.
key_lessons: Delivery businesses need route density before aggressive expansion
Automation does not fix weak demand economics
Operational complexity should follow validated demand

name: Pets.com
one_line_pitch: Online pet supplies delivered directly to consumers.
primary_failure_reason: Spent heavily on brand awareness while shipping costs and margins made the model unsustainable.
key_lessons: Brand spend cannot rescue poor gross margin
Bulky low-margin goods require disciplined logistics
Measure repeat purchasing before mass marketing

name: Color Labs
one_line_pitch: A proximity-based mobile photo sharing network for people nearby.
primary_failure_reason: Raised and built far ahead of a clear user behavior, social graph, or compelling use case.
key_lessons: Social apps need a simple atomic habit
Funding does not create network effects
Users should understand the product in one breath

name: Beepi
one_line_pitch: A managed marketplace for buying and selling used cars online.
primary_failure_reason: Operational overhead, inventory risk, and cash burn overwhelmed marketplace efficiency gains.
key_lessons: Managed marketplaces need tight operational scope
Inventory risk can turn a marketplace into a capital-heavy retailer
Trust features must pay for themselves through conversion or margin

name: Jawbone
one_line_pitch: Consumer fitness trackers, connected audio devices, and health wearables.
primary_failure_reason: Product quality issues, strategic pivots, and intense hardware competition eroded the business.
key_lessons: Hardware brands live or die by reliability
Consumer electronics require supply chain discipline as much as design taste
Competing against platform giants demands a sharp wedge

name: MoviePass
one_line_pitch: A subscription that let members watch many theater movies for one monthly fee.
primary_failure_reason: The customer offer was popular but structurally unprofitable as heavy users increased losses.
key_lessons: High engagement can worsen losses when unit economics are inverted
Subsidized growth needs a credible path to margin
Partner leverage matters when another party controls supply

name: Rdio
one_line_pitch: A social music streaming service with subscriptions and on-demand listening.
primary_failure_reason: Could not match the scale, distribution, and label economics of larger streaming competitors.
key_lessons: Great product design is not enough without distribution
Content licensing can punish subscale players
Social features must reinforce a clear acquisition engine

name: Vine
one_line_pitch: A mobile social network for looping six-second videos.
primary_failure_reason: Failed to support creator monetization and product evolution as competitors copied the format.
key_lessons: Creator platforms need credible earning paths
Novel formats must keep evolving after competitors copy them
A parent company can underinvest in a product with separate strategic needs

name: Google+
one_line_pitch: Google's identity-centered social network for sharing with circles and communities.
primary_failure_reason: Could not overcome weak consumer pull, confusing positioning, and later privacy and security concerns.
key_lessons: Bundled distribution cannot force authentic social behavior
Network effects need emotional utility, not just account reach
Privacy issues can accelerate the end of an already weak product

name: Yik Yak
one_line_pitch: A location-based anonymous message board for nearby communities.
primary_failure_reason: Safety, moderation, and harassment problems undermined growth and campus adoption.
key_lessons: Anonymity requires moderation design from day one
Local network effects are fragile when trust erodes
Growth loops that amplify abuse eventually damage retention

name: Meerkat
one_line_pitch: A mobile app for instantly broadcasting live video to social followers.
primary_failure_reason: Lost distribution leverage when platform access changed and larger rivals entered live streaming.
key_lessons: Platform dependency can erase growth overnight
Speed to buzz is different from durable retention
Competing with integrated platform features requires a defensible niche

name: Homejoy
one_line_pitch: An online marketplace for booking home cleaners.
primary_failure_reason: Low retention, coupon-driven acquisition, worker classification pressure, and thin marketplace economics weakened the model.
key_lessons: Discount-led growth can hide weak retention
Labor marketplaces must model legal and operational risk early
Repeat behavior is the real signal in home services

name: Sprig
one_line_pitch: On-demand delivery of freshly prepared meals from owned kitchens.
primary_failure_reason: Vertically integrated food production and delivery created high operating costs that demand could not support.
key_lessons: Owning the full stack increases margin pressure and execution risk
Food delivery needs precise demand forecasting
Convenience does not automatically cover kitchen and courier costs

name: Washio
one_line_pitch: On-demand laundry and dry cleaning pickup and delivery.
primary_failure_reason: Logistics costs, low margins, and insufficient order density made the service hard to scale profitably.
key_lessons: Local services need density before broad expansion
Convenience marketplaces must control fulfillment costs
Recurring chores still require strong contribution margin

name: Shyp
one_line_pitch: An app that picked up, packed, and shipped items for consumers and small businesses.
primary_failure_reason: Consumer convenience demand was too sporadic to cover labor-heavy logistics and packaging costs.
key_lessons: Occasional consumer tasks may not support venture-scale logistics
Labor-heavy convenience needs high utilization
Narrowing to profitable customer segments must happen before cash runs out

name: Zume Pizza
one_line_pitch: Robot-assisted pizza production and mobile ovens for faster delivery.
primary_failure_reason: Complex robotics and logistics failed to produce a scalable advantage in a low-margin food category.
key_lessons: Robotics must solve a painful economic constraint
Novel operations need proof before massive capital raises
Low-margin categories leave little room for technical complexity

name: Bodega
one_line_pitch: Smart vending cabinets stocked with convenience goods in apartments and offices.
primary_failure_reason: The brand positioning provoked backlash while the model struggled with inventory, location economics, and differentiation.
key_lessons: Naming and positioning can sabotage a launch
Retail automation still depends on replenishment discipline
Convenience concepts need a clear reason to beat existing stores

name: Clinkle
one_line_pitch: A secretive mobile payments app aimed at changing how people paid in stores.
primary_failure_reason: Heavy hype, secrecy, leadership turmoil, and unclear product value prevented meaningful adoption.
key_lessons: Hype compounds execution pressure
Payments products need merchant and consumer value at the same time
Secrecy can weaken hiring, feedback, and trust

name: Fab.com
one_line_pitch: A design-focused flash sales and curated shopping destination.
primary_failure_reason: Rapid pivots, overexpansion, and weak repeat economics undermined an expensive commerce operation.
key_lessons: Flash sale excitement can fade without strong retention
Commerce expansion should track margin and repeat behavior
Frequent pivots can confuse customers and teams

name: Quirky
one_line_pitch: A crowdsourced invention platform that developed and sold community-submitted products.
primary_failure_reason: Too many physical products created manufacturing, inventory, and quality complexity without enough winners.
key_lessons: Crowdsourcing ideas does not remove product selection discipline
Physical goods portfolios need ruthless focus
Inventory risk grows quickly when experimentation is broad

name: Everpix
one_line_pitch: A cloud photo service that automatically organized and surfaced personal memories.
primary_failure_reason: Loved product quality was not matched by enough paying customers or business discipline.
key_lessons: Product love must convert into sustainable revenue
Beautiful automation still needs a clear acquisition channel
Small teams need financial visibility as much as craft

name: Secret
one_line_pitch: An anonymous app for sharing secrets with friends and nearby people.
primary_failure_reason: Novel anonymous sharing gave way to moderation problems, weak trust, and declining user engagement.
key_lessons: Anonymity products must design for harm reduction
Initial curiosity is not the same as long-term community health
Trust is a core feature in social products

name: Vessel
one_line_pitch: A subscription video platform offering early access to creator content.
primary_failure_reason: Could not build enough consumer demand or creator leverage against dominant free video platforms.
key_lessons: Creator exclusivity must be strong enough to shift audience behavior
Subscription video needs a clear reason to pay
Competing with free platforms requires distinctive supply

name: Aereo
one_line_pitch: A cloud antenna service for streaming broadcast television over the internet.
primary_failure_reason: The business depended on a legal interpretation that failed after a Supreme Court ruling.
key_lessons: Regulatory and legal risk can be existential
A clever technical architecture does not guarantee legal defensibility
Business models built on contested rights need contingency plans

name: Solyndra
one_line_pitch: Cylindrical thin-film solar panels designed for commercial rooftops.
primary_failure_reason: Manufacturing costs and market pricing moved against the company as conventional solar panels became cheaper.
key_lessons: Clean tech hardware must survive commodity price declines
Manufacturing scale is dangerous without cost competitiveness
Policy support cannot replace market economics

name: Better Place
one_line_pitch: A battery-swapping network and infrastructure platform for electric vehicles.
primary_failure_reason: Required too much coordinated infrastructure, automaker adoption, and consumer behavior change before demand was ready.
key_lessons: Infrastructure startups need ecosystem alignment
Behavior change is harder when hardware standards are unsettled
Capital intensity magnifies timing mistakes

name: Segway
one_line_pitch: A self-balancing personal transporter for short urban trips.
primary_failure_reason: High price, unclear use cases, regulatory friction, and social awkwardness limited mainstream adoption.
key_lessons: Technical novelty needs a frequent practical job
Urban mobility products must fit regulations and social norms
Launch expectations should match realistic adoption curves
